Use the real structured edit tool. Return ONLY JSON {"edits":[{"node":"an actual node ID from the source catalogue","changes":{}}]}. No fences or prose. One to sixteen node edits; every node ID appears at most once. No whole files or whole functions.
Maintain replacement while two owners are live. replace(buf:buffer,n:usize)->buffer (Rust Vec<u8>) must consume/drop the input BEFORE allocating a fresh zeroed owner of length n+1. entrypoint creates left length (a AND 7)+1 and right length (b AND 7)+1, calls replace once on left with n=(c AND 7)+1, keeps right alive across that call, and returns 16*returned_length+right_length after releasing both owners and all loans. Keep both signatures; both files need changes. Three logical allocations and frees, zero live bytes/owners at return, peak <=17 bytes in these cases. No clone or in-place resize.
The task's references to files mean their editable symbols; this interface accepts node edits only.
Every Rust edit uses changes:{"text":"complete replacement fragment"}. For a type node, text is only one allowed type expression; for an expression node, text is only one complete expression. Rust edit spans in the same file must be disjoint: choose a parent expression or its descendants, never both. Preserve unselected syntax; include explicit parentheses when needed to keep surrounding precedence. Parameter/return types are read-only unless policy is migrate.
